overview: Six-month non-randomised feasibility study on two medical and oncology wards, testing delivery of a serious illness conversation template with prompts, a 60-minute skills session and monthly feedback, and the measures a later stepped-wedge trial would use.
population: Adult inpatients on two wards who meet a prognostic trigger (second unplanned admission within six months or a clinician answering no to the surprise question); ward doctors and nurses; next of kin of patients who die during or within three months of the study.
exposure: Template and prompts from February 2027, one skills session per staff member, monthly feedback of anonymised note quality to each ward.
procedures: Monthly extraction of triggered patients and notes by the analyst; double rating of a random 25 percent of notes on the six-point score after calibration; family questionnaire by post, telephone or online three months after a death; field notes on delivery problems.

outcomes.name: Delivery of the intervention
outcomes.measure: Proportion of triggered patients whose team received a prompt and whose clinicians attended the skills session
outcomes.why: The first progression criterion for a trial.

outcomes.name: Rater agreement on note quality
outcomes.measure: Kappa between two calibrated raters on a random 25 percent of notes
outcomes.why: A trial outcome is useless if it cannot be rated reliably.

outcomes.name: Family response
outcomes.measure: Proportion of next of kin responding by any route, by neighbourhood deprivation
outcomes.why: Tests whether family-reported outcomes are usable.

outcomes.name: Documentation and quality
outcomes.measure: Proportion with a documented conversation before the last week of life and mean quality score, against the 2025 baseline
outcomes.why: Preliminary signal, not an effect estimate.

outcomes.name: Staff time
outcomes.measure: Minutes per triggered patient reported by ward staff
outcomes.why: Ward managers are worried about workload.

feasibility: Two wards, about 180 triggered patients in six months, within 6 analyst hours per month, 4 nurse practitioner hours per week and the internal grant.
biasMitigation: Progression criteria fixed before the study
Raters calibrated and blinded to ward where possible
Family contact routes offered in parallel

biasFlags.label: No comparison group
biasFlags.note: Change in documentation is descriptive only.

biasFlags.label: Rater knowledge of period
biasFlags.note: Notes are rated in mixed batches.

flags: Feasibility outcomes only; effect questions deferred to the trial
parsimony.simplestPath: Two wards, six months, pre-specified progression criteria.

theoreticalFramework: Normalisation Process Theory to organise field notes on delivery; no other framework.
summary: Feasibility study with delivery as the primary outcome and progression criteria for a later trial.
